q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 17: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
1. Statical refraction

  • A)Hypemetropia
  • the image of an object form behind the retina
  • only by accommodation can be brought on the retina

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 19: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Classification of hypermetropia

  • etiology:
  • Axial
  • the anteroposterior axis is too short;
  • Index
  • refraction of the ocular media is lower than normal;
  • Curvature
  • the corneal curvature is reduced
  • Decreased refractive power

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 23: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Management

  • Optical,
  • spherical convergent glasses.
  • the strongest convergent glasses that the patient is able to achieve maximum VA.
  • Addition for near vision to substitute the missing accommodation.
  • In children a total correction is needed to prevent strabismus.
  • soft contact lenses.
  • Correction of aphakia

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 24: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Management

  • Surgical,
  • excimer laser
  • may correct an up to 6 D hypermetropia.
  • Correction of aphakia

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 25: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
B)Myopia

  • A discrepancy between the refractive power and axial length of the eye
  • parallel incident light rays converge at a focal point anterior to the retina
  • The myopic eye can only produce sharply defined images of close objects from which the light rays diverge until they enter the eye

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 27: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Classification  of myopia

  • etiology:
  • axial
  • the anteroposterior axis of the globe longer than normal;
  • index
  • the refractive index of the ocular media greater than normal
  • curvature
  • the corneal curvature is increased.

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 45: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Pathological astigmatism

  • Optical
  • a Cylinder lenses refract light only in the plane perpendicular to the axis of the cylinder.
  • The axis of the cylinder defines the nonrefracting plane.
  • b–d Cylinder lenses
  • plus cylinders (c)
  • minus cylinders (d).

q: Lecture 2 – Refraction – slide 48: what does this picture show? Describe it.
a:
Irregular astigmatism

  • irregularities at the same median of the ocular dioptric system that result in areas with different refractions
  • Corneal ulcerations with resulting scarring of the cornea.
  • Penetrating corneal trauma.
  • Advanced keratoconus
  • Curvature and refractive power of the refractive media are totally irregular,
  • multiple focal points.
